Architecture overview ​

Alloq is a resource planning app for software teams. It is written in Python with Reflex 0.10.0, which builds a React frontend from Python code and runs the event handlers in a Python backend. The data lives in PostgreSQL. The same code runs as a web app and as a macOS desktop app.

This page describes the system from the outside in. It uses the C4 levels:

  • Context. Who uses Alloq and which other systems it talks to.
  • Containers. The programs that run and the data store.
  • Components. The Python packages inside the app.

The last section follows one request from a page to the database. The layers page then explains each layer in the code.

System context ​

Four kinds of people use Alloq. The personas come from the roles in roles.py (PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE, EMPLOYEE_ROLE) and the admin switch of appkit-user.

  • Administrator. An appkit user with the admin switch. Administrators can do everything, including the pages under "Administration".
  • Project manager. A user with the role project_manager ("Projektmanager"). Project managers read and edit planning, projects and team, but they have no administration.
  • Employee. A user with the role employee ("Mitarbeiter" [employee]). Employees can only read the projects page and the resource planning.
  • Desktop user. Any of the three above who uses the desktop app. The desktop user signs in with Microsoft Entra ID and connects to Postgres with a personal token.

Editable source: system-context.drawio

The base configuration configuration/config.yaml lists one OAuth provider, azure. A GitHub provider is in the file but commented out. The desktop sign-in is described on the desktop page.

Containers ​

Alloq has two ways to run the same Python code.

  • Web app. The Reflex backend runs on a server (backend port 3030 in config.yaml, workers: 2). It serves the compiled frontend below the path /alloq (frontend_path). Users open it in a browser. The browser talks to the backend over a websocket. Every click that needs data sends an event over this websocket to a state class in the backend.
  • Desktop app. A Tauri shell in tauri/ starts the same Python backend inside the app process. main.rs runs it on a background thread bound to 127.0.0.1:18442 (BACKEND_PORT) and shows the prebuilt frontend in a webview. The app carries no secrets. Each person signs in with Entra ID and connects to Postgres with their own token.
  • PostgreSQL. One database holds the Alloq tables and the appkit-user tables. The web app connects with the credentials from the secret: entries in config.yaml. The desktop app connects with the Entra token of the signed-in person.

Editable source: deployment-modes.drawio

The configuration profiles that select these modes are listed in the configuration reference.

The diagram shows the same containers, with the components inside the Reflex app.

Components: the package split ​

The code is a uv workspace. The host app and four packages are members. The workspace is declared in pyproject.toml under [tool.uv.workspace] with members = ["components/*"].

PackagePathWhat it holds
Host appapp/Entry point app/app.py, admin pages in app/pages/, the sidebar in app/components/sidebar.py, desktop code in app/desktop/, configuration in app/configuration.py
alloq-commonscomponents/alloq-commonsEntities, models, repositories, shared services (utilization.py, quick_project.py, daily_rate_pricing.py), shared UI (shell.py, list_view.py, toolbar.py, excel_grid/), roles.py, access.py, theme.py, and the department, role, daily rate and holiday states
alloq-teamcomponents/alloq-teamTeam page (/team), employee table, cards, inspector and form, TeamState
alloq-projectcomponents/alloq-projectProjects page (/projects), planning page (/ and /plan), planning grid, Gantt view, plan modal, forecast and plan distribution services
alloq-dashboardcomponents/alloq-dashboardDashboard page (/dashboard), KPI cards, portfolio, drill-down drawers, aggregation services

Each feature package has the same folders: components/, services/, states/ and a pages.py with a page factory. The host app calls every page factory once in app/app.py and passes it the sidebar.

All packages also use the appkit libraries from PyPI: appkit-commons (database session, base repository, configuration, service registry), appkit-user (users, sign-in, sessions, requires_admin), appkit-mantine (UI components) and appkit-ui. Their versions are pinned in pyproject.toml.

Dependency direction ​

Editable source: package-split.drawio

The arrows point from the package that imports to the package it imports. These are the rules:

  • No package in components/ may import the host app app. The test tests/test_component_boundaries.py (test_components_do_not_import_host_app) parses every .py file under components/*/src/ and fails if it finds import app or from app....
  • The same test file checks that app.roles.ALL_ROLES is the same object as alloq_commons.roles.ALL_ROLES (test_app_roles_reexports_commons_roles). The host app re-exports the roles and does not define its own.
  • alloq_commons imports no feature package. Its pyproject.toml lists no workspace dependencies.
  • alloq_team depends only on alloq_commons (pyproject.toml).
  • alloq_project depends on alloq_commons and alloq_team (pyproject.toml). The planning grid and Gantt view reuse the absence dialog absence_modal and TeamState from alloq_team, e.g. in planning_absence_state.py.
  • alloq_dashboard declares alloq-project and alloq-team in its pyproject.toml. In the code it imports ProjectState and project_card from alloq_project, e.g. in project_cards.py.

Only the first rule has a test. The direction between the feature packages is kept by the pyproject.toml dependencies and by review.
